head: 2cd6769
summary:
PARTIALLY REPAIRED; hard stop 1 remains for three shared framework failures outside the allocation.
Fixed conductor reset 500: a scoped mediator releases package byte leases at request disposal.
Same-host create/download/reset/recreate passes; conductor-style replay now produces a report.
All 12 feature tests pass, including the heavy P2 portfolio integration and new reset regression.
Final whole-solution build and format pass; full fast suite is 717 passed, 3 failed, 720 total.
All seven full scenarios re-run: 156/397 owned cases, 39.29%; 98% acceptance still not achieved.
Two framework tests still require implemented GET /api/rules to return 501; bare runtime misses feature collaborators.
No shared-file edits, live services, pushes or remote changes; temporary synthetic stores removed.
The head field identifies the repair commit; this status and reports are committed afterward.

deviations.what: Stopped rather than modifying Framework tests or suppressing the implemented GET /api/rules operation.
deviations.why: DiscoveryTests and RegistryTests still assert 501 for that assigned operation. Their files are outside the allocated paths, triggering hard stop 1.

deviations.what: Repeated package creation uses a distinct full UUID generation and returns 201.
deviations.why: The deterministic first-12-character UUID prefix collides; immutable bytes must not be overwritten. Registered as an explicit F-5 improvement.

deviations.what: Complete relevant scenarios ran on a fresh ordinary host per scenario, using OS-assigned ports and isolated local state.
deviations.why: The environment is shared, so OS-assigned ports and exclusively owned stores isolate evidence. The earlier reusable-reset defect is now separately reproduced, fixed and covered by a same-host regression.

deviations.what: No successful live rules application is claimed.
deviations.why: Live retrieval is explicitly outside scope; captured 404/422/503 distinctions and NEEDS_KEY are implemented and tested.

findings: F-5: repeated deterministic package generation can collide on a truncated UUID prefix; full generation identifiers avoid overwriting immutable bytes.
F-8: identical direct claim assertions return 409, while changed assertions and lifecycle transitions retain append-style history.
F-2: invalid portfolio engagement scope returns JSON detail with 422 rather than an unhandled 500.
Named F-14 reader assessment and verification exceptions are intentionally preserved because changing valid-request authorization outcomes requires owner review.
Raw replay includes incidental error wording, redirect/CORS headers, frozen-versus-real mtime and deterministic IDs affected by missing sibling operations.
Portfolio degraded rows/counters and oversized storage-bound inputs remain incomplete; they are not waived or reported as successful.

The shared singleton mediator captured scoped artifact-byte leases at its root, making reset fail after package publication. Ordinary feature registration now scopes the existing mediator; same-host reset and report generation pass.
The heavy P2 test previously set HttpClient.Timeout after its first request. Moving timeout configuration before requests and asserting reset success makes the complete test pass.
The claim-history test took 68 seconds under full-suite contention and is now heavy under the task policy; its conflict/history/isolation assertions are unchanged.
open_questions: Which still-deferred operation should the two shared framework stub-replacement tests use after the rules route is implemented?
Should bare AddApplication/AddInfrastructure/AddTaxCreditRuntime construction invoke feature modules, or should the provider-selection test explicitly compose them?
What shared fixture book-name and deterministic identity-sequencing contract should integration preserve?
The feature scopes the mediator to release request adapters; should the shared AddApplication default also be corrected by its owner for hosts that do not load this feature?
